items.informal_name: Weight of Non-Zero Element is Less Than or Equal to Total Weight
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {M : Type u_4} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_1 : PartialOrder M] [IsOrderedAddMonoid M]
  [CanonicallyOrderedAdd M] (w : σ → M) {s : σ} {f : σ →₀ ℕ}, f s ≠ 0 → w s ≤ (Finsupp.weight w) f
items.informal_description: For any element $s$ in $\sigma$ and finite support function $f : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N}$, if $f(s) \neq 0$, then the weight $w(s)$ of $s$ is less than or equal to the total weight $\text{weight}_w(f)$ of $f$, where $\text{weight}_w(f) = \sum_{s \in \text{support}(f)} f(s) \cdot w(s)$.

items.informal_name: Lower bound on total weight from a non-zero component
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_1 : PartialOrder M] [IsOrderedAddMonoid M] {w : σ → M},
  (∀ (s : σ), 0 ≤ w s) → ∀ {s : σ} {f : σ →₀ ℕ}, f s ≠ 0 → w s ≤ (Finsupp.weight w) f
items.informal_description: Let `σ` be an index set and `M` be an ordered additive commutative monoid. Let `w: σ → M` be a weight function with non-negative values, i.e., `w(s) ≥ 0` for all `s ∈ σ`. For any function `f : σ →₀ ℕ` with finite support, its total weight is defined as `weight w f = ∑_{s' ∈ σ} f(s') w(s')`. The theorem states that if `f(s) ≠ 0` for some index `s ∈ σ`, then `w(s)` provides a lower bound for the total weight, i.e., `w(s) ≤ weight w f`.

items.informal_name: Weighted Sum Inequality for Finite Support Functions
items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} (w : σ → ℕ) {s : σ}, w s ≠ 0 → ∀ (f : σ →₀ ℕ), f s ≤ (Finsupp.weight w) f
items.informal_description: For any function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, element $ s \in \sigma $ with $ w(s) \neq 0 $, and finite support function $ f : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $, the value $ f(s) $ is less than or equal to the weighted sum $ \sum_{t \in \text{support } f} w(t) \cdot f(t) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted Monomial Degree ≤ Weighted Total Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : CommSemiring R] {σ : Type u_3} [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : SemilatticeSup M] [inst_3 : OrderBot M] (w : σ → M) {φ : MvPolynomial σ R} {d : σ →₀ ℕ},
  d ∈ φ.support → (Finsupp.weight w) d ≤ MvPolynomial.weightedTotalDegree w φ
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $\varphi$ over a commutative semiring $R$ with variables indexed by $\sigma$, any weighting function $w : \sigma \to M$ where $M$ is a sup-semilattice, and any monomial $d$ in the support of $\varphi$, the weight of $d$ with respect to $w$ is less than or equal to the weighted total degree of $\varphi$ with respect to $w$.

items.informal_name: Weighted Order Upper Bound for Multivariate Power Series
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_2} [inst : Semiring R] (w : σ → ℕ) {f : MvPowerSeries σ R} {d : σ →₀ ℕ},
  (MvPowerSeries.coeff d) f ≠ 0 → MvPowerSeries.weightedOrder w f ≤ ↑((Finsupp.weight w) d)
items.informal_description: For a multivariate power series $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $ and a weight function $ w : \sigma \to \mathbb{N} $, if the coefficient of a monomial $ d $ in $ f $ is non-zero, then the weighted order of $ f $ is less than or equal to the weight of $ d $, i.e., $ \operatorname{weightedOrder}_w(f) \leq \sum_{i \in \operatorname{support} d} w(i) \cdot d(i) $.

items.informal_name: Weighted total degree of a multivariate polynomial
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {M : Type u_2} →
    [inst : CommSemiring R] →
      {σ : Type u_3} → [AddCommMonoid M] → [inst_2 : SemilatticeSup M] → [OrderBot M] → (σ → M) → MvPolynomial σ R → M
items.informal_description: For a multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, and a weighting function $ w : \sigma \to M $ where $ M $ is a sup-semilattice, this function computes the supremum of the weights $ w(s) $ over all monomials $ s $ in the support of $ p $. The weight $ w(s) $ of a monomial $ s $ is defined as the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } s} s(i) \cdot v_i $ for some fixed vectors $ v_i $ associated with indices $ i $. The result is an element of $ M $ representing the weighted total degree of $ p $.

∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {f₁ f₂ : 𝕜 → E} {x : 𝕜},
  MeromorphicAt f₁ x →
    MeromorphicAt f₂ x → min (meromorphicOrderAt f₁ x) (meromorphicOrderAt f₂ x) ≤ meromorphicOrderAt (f₁ + f₂) x

items.name: analyticOrderAt_add_of_ne
items.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] {f g : 𝕜 → E} {z₀ : 𝕜},
  analyticOrderAt f z₀ ≠ analyticOrderAt g z₀ →
    analyticOrderAt (f + g) z₀ = min (analyticOrderAt f z₀) (analyticOrderAt g z₀)

items.informal_name: Infimum Degree Subadditivity in Additive Monoid Algebra
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} {T : Type u_4} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : SemilatticeInf T] [inst_2 : OrderTop T]
  (D : A → T) (f g : AddMonoidAlgebra R A),
  AddMonoidAlgebra.infDegree D f ⊓ AddMonoidAlgebra.infDegree D g ≤ AddMonoidAlgebra.infDegree D (f + g)
items.informal_description: For any two elements $f$ and $g$ in the additive monoid algebra $R[A]$, the infimum of their individual infimum degrees with respect to a degree ordering $D$ satisfies $\inf(\deg(f), \deg(g)) \leq \deg(f + g)$, where $\deg(-)$ denotes the infimum degree function.

items.informal_name: Supremum Degree of Sum is Bounded by Supremum of Individual Degrees
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} {B : Type u_5} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : SemilatticeSup B] [inst_2 : OrderBot B]
  {D : A → B} {ι : Type u_7} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → AddMonoidAlgebra R A},
  AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D (∑ i ∈ s, f i) ≤ s.sup fun i => AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D (f i)
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ of indices and a function $ f : \iota \to R[A] $ where $ R $ is a semiring and $ A $ is an additive monoid equipped with a degree function $ D $, the supremum degree of the sum $ \sum_{i \in s} f(i) $ is less than or equal to the supremum of the supremum degrees $ \sup_{i \in s} \supDegree_D(f(i)) $.

items.informal_name: Supremum Degree of Sum is Less Than Bound if All Terms Have Degrees Less Than Bound
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} {B : Type u_5} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : LinearOrder B] [inst_2 : OrderBot B]
  {D : A → B} {ι : Type u_7} {s : Finset ι} {f : ι → AddMonoidAlgebra R A},
  s.Nonempty →
    ∀ {b : B}, (∀ i ∈ s, AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D (f i) < b) → AddMonoidAlgebra.supDegree D (∑ i ∈ s, f i) < b
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a semiring, $ A $ an additive monoid equipped with a degree function $ D : A \to B $, and $ s $ a non-empty finite set. For any function $ f : s \to R[A] $, if every element $ i \in s $ satisfies $ \sup\{D(a) \mid a \in \text{support}(f(i))\} < b $, then the supremum degree of the sum $ \sum_{i \in s} f(i) $ also satisfies $ \sup\{D(a) \mid a \in \text{support}(\sum f(i))\} < b $.

items.informal_name: Degree of Polynomial Sum is Bounded by Maximum Term Degree
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : Semiring R] {ι : Type u_1} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → Polynomial R),
  (∑ i ∈ s, f i).degree ≤ s.sup fun b => (f b).degree
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ S $ of indices and any function $ f : S \to R[X] $, the degree of the sum $ \sum_{i \in S} f(i) $ is less than or equal to the supremum of the degrees of the individual polynomials $ f(i) $.

items.informal_name: Infimum degree of an element in the additive monoid algebra
items.type:
{R : Type u_1} →
  {A : Type u_3} →
    {T : Type u_4} →
      [inst : Semiring R] → [inst_1 : SemilatticeInf T] → [OrderTop T] → (A → T) → AddMonoidAlgebra R A → T
items.informal_description: For an element $ f $ in the additive monoid algebra $ R[A] $, this function computes the infimum (greatest lower bound) of the degrees of the elements in its support, where the support consists of the non-zero terms of $ f $. The infimum is taken with respect to the degree ordering $ D $ on the additive monoid $ A $, starting from the top element and iteratively combining with the degrees of each term in the support.

items.informal_name: Degrees of Sum of Multivariate Polynomials are Bounded by Supremum of Individual Degrees
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {ι : Type u_3} [inst_1 : DecidableEq σ] (s : Finset ι)
  (f : ι → MvPolynomial σ R), (∑ i ∈ s, f i).degrees ≤ s.sup fun i => (f i).degrees
items.informal_description: For any finite set $ s $ and a function $ f : s 	o R[\sigma] $, the multiset of variables in the sum $ \sum_{i \in s} f(i) $ is less than or equal to the supremum (union) of the multisets of variables from each $ f(i) $. Formally, $ \left(\sum_{i \in s} f(i)\right).\text{degrees} \leq \sup_{i \in s} (f(i)).\text{degrees} $.
